content.text: No disclaimer of implied warranties exists anywhere, so the express warranty is not swallowed. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
input.rationale: Section 12 gives an express conformance-to-Specifications warranty for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and continuing for as long as the Software remains under Maintenance Services — this meets and in fact exceeds the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no additional charge under the Software Repair Service (p0077), and during the acceptance period Sparkling may reject the Software with a full refund of all amounts paid (§§ 7–8, p0057). Critically, the document contains no disclaimer of implied warranties or "AS IS" language, so nothing swallows the express warranty, and § 15 preserves recovery of direct damages. Noted but not flagged as deviations (minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording): there is no separate "professional and workmanlike manner" warranty for the installation/conversion/training services, no compliance-with-laws warranty, and no no-malicious-code warranty; the repair obligation is also framed as "best efforts" rather than an unqualified repair/replace/refund election. These are sub-elements only — the material terms (period and remedy) sit at or above the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.
